hypothesis: Existing accepted points include ground incorrectly above the fixed .05m floor boundary. Qualifying new positive-height points with their existing one-pixel range sensitivity may change early risk maps/routes and prevent stalled navigation. Saved-trajectory filtering alone does not unblock the terminal root; navigation improvement is unproven.
mechanism: After the unchanged paired texture and height filtering, admit a NEW occupied point only if world_z - existing sigma_m > .05. Aligned fields preserved; ambiguous points remain unknown. Existing confirmed risks, TTL and planning clearance are unchanged.
inputs: Only current causal binocular packet world coordinates, sigma_m, paired RGB/texture, disparity and current native IMU encoder registration. Same forward60cm rig as measured control; no additional geometry change.

control.limitations: Historical same-configuration development E2; RGB may differ, no complete causal A/B or heldout claim. Forward rig remains navigation rejected; reused fixed research sensor platform only.

qualification: 4CPU checks passed. Full saved accepted-surface replay must match implemented predicate and preserve clocks/pixel alignment/history. No online renderer truth.
navigation_gate: E2 actual success within90s, raw final distance<=.2m, all contacts available and no contact, valid source clocks/registration and request execution, two fully decoded videos, unchanged depth gate. Only then E0/E1, otherwise stop and close unused budget.
online_depth_gate: Same conditional confident0.5-3m depth accuracy: >=1000 comparable pixels,p90<=.15m, fraction error>.3m<=.1; truth only scoring; not whole coverage.
fixed: Rig, masks, SGBM, lighting, scene,90s, IMU/encoder source and privileged initial gauge/ideal lowlevelIMU, floor/safe-start/controlled-unknown priors, memory lifecycle, planner, clearance, control and gains unchanged.
stop: Reject on navigation/source/execution failure, no sigma multiplier tuning or alternate floor thresholds. Closed camera/control/data budgets stay closed.
